Country.evidence_source: The experience of university life in the UK is commonly identified as a move away from home to independence in that it offers many young people their first opportunity to live outside the family and away from the restrictions of school attendance.

Type.evidence_source: The research described here highlighted the extent to which the experience of transition served as a context for young suicide in higher education.

Area.evidence_source: Transition exposes young people to a range of risks and HEIs have recognised these and offer a range of services aimed at managing them. The research described here highlighted the extent to which the experience of transition served as a context for young suicide in higher education. Transition emerged both as a particularly strong feature of the HE environment at certain times in the academic year and as an inner psychological state which characterised the accounts of student suicide. --- HEIs in the UK have acknowledged the stresses and demands intrinsic to this period of transition and they provide a range of support and advice services which include supervised accommodation, financial advice and support, health services, counselling services, careers guidance, services for international students and disability services.
